dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Inspects both graph pairs (sizes, headers, line counts), previews the reference alignment, recognizes it covers all 2379 yeast nodes and copies it — exploiting the reference for NC. Characterizes node-name convention (numeric Entrez IDs, no exact overlap).

Builds an S3 evaluator and tests baseline heuristics (node order, degree-sort), quantifying them at ~0.01 and concluding they cannot clear the 0.32 threshold — baseline quantification per level-10 anchor.

Recognizes S3 as a local edge-conservation objective (writes C++ simulated annealing), then researches biological orthology (HomoloGene/MyGene) as an NC/seed signal and tests it — distinguishing topology (S3) from name/reference signal (NC).
Identifies SANA as the published tool purpose-built to optimize S3, downloads and builds it — selecting a known-reasonable method with explicit rationale tied to the metric.
Runs SANA with pure S3 objective and monitors scores (0.19→0.24), reasoning about calibration vs optimization time — evaluating method fit against the concrete instance.
Extended terminal-wedge recovery loop; no further orientation content — confirms the substantive orientation was front-loaded in steps 2-27.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically characterized each network pair (sizes, format, Entrez-ID naming), inspected the reference alignment and exploited it for the yeast deliverable, and explicitly separated the topology signal (S3) from name-overlap/reference signal (NC) — squarely matching anchor 8. It also hit several level-10 markers: it quantified baseline scores (~0.01), identified the structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluated multiple methods (own SA, HomoloGene orthology, SANA), and derived a targeted per-deliverable strategy. It falls just short of 10 because the method evaluation was iterative rather than a systematic upfront survey of published methods against instance size/runtime, placing it at 9.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Immediately separated the two deliverables with their distinct thresholds; solved yeast via the perfect alignment (recognizing NC+S3 satisfied) and isolated DM-HS as the hard S3-only sub-goal — difficulty-aware effort budgeting across deliverables.
Built a Python S3 scorer as a prerequisite milestone before attempting optimization — sensible sequencing of 'build the scorer before optimizing against it'.
Measured baseline heuristics (~0.01) and orthology seed (~0.0135) as explicit numeric done-checks, escalating through ordered fallback approaches (heuristic → orthology → SANA).
Ran SANA while tracking S3 progress (0.19→0.22→0.24) explicitly against the 0.32 target, gating each next action on the measured score vs threshold.

Trajectory collapsed into environmental terminal-recovery attempts; agent kept restating an accurate milestone/state summary but produced no further decomposition work — abandonment was forced by the wedged PTY, not a chosen discard of the plan.

dimensions.reasoning: In its productive phase the agent hit anchor 8: explicit ordered milestones (parse → build S3 scorer → baseline measurement → optimize to the 0.32 threshold), each with a numeric done-criterion, and both deliverables tracked distinctly with their own thresholds. It also showed touches of the 10 anchor — difficulty-aware budgeting (trivially solving yeast, focusing on fly), fallback branches (heuristic→orthology→SANA→param tuning), and score-gating before advancing — but the milestones were emergent per-step rather than a crisp pre-designed hierarchy, so it falls short of 9-10. The long wedged tail neither adds nor subtracts milestone quality since the plan wasn't voluntarily abandoned.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Built /app/test_dm_align.py that reads DM/HS and computes S3 for several candidate mappings; reported 'best S3 about 0.01', showing a real (not proxy) S3 implementation actually run on alignments.
C++ aligner 'maintains Ea and induced HS edge count incrementally' — the S3 objective is faithfully encoded internally as the optimization target.
Computed S3 (~0.0135) on the HomoloGene-seeded DM-HS alignment, confirming continued use of a local S3 scorer to reject weak candidates.
For yeast, copied y2kr-SC-perfect.align assuming NC≈1.0 and adequate S3 — never implemented NC, never scored the reference to confirm NC=1.0 or check S3, no sanity-check of a scorer.

For DM-HS topology optimization it trusted SANA's internally-reported S3 (0.19→0.24) rather than re-scoring outputs with its own implementation; SANA was killed before writing output, so no final self-score occurred.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent implemented a faithful S3 scorer and ran it on multiple candidate alignments (above anchor 3's 'rough proxy'), but it never implemented NC — it simply copied the reference alignment on faith — and showed no explicit injectivity/coverage/exact-format validation or reference-based sanity check of its scorer (below anchor 5's full spec compliance and well below the reference-cross-checking of 8). This places observed behavior at 4: a real S3 measurement loop for DM-HS, but incomplete coverage of the specified metrics and no scorer validation.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Tracks S3 across multiple approaches (degree/order ~0.01, C++ SA ~0.017, HomoloGene ~0.0135) always against the 0.32 target, and consistently knows yeast is done vs DM-HS short — continuity of best-so-far, not isolated numbers.
Logs SANA's live S3 progression (0.19→0.219→0.231→0.241) over minutes, distinguishes slow convergence from stuck, and recognizes it likely won't reach target.
Detects the calibration-heavy run is wasting time / plateauing at ~0.24 and decides to stop the approach rather than loop indefinitely.

Throughout the long terminal-wedge ordeal, accurately restates best-so-far per deliverable (yeast complete; DM-HS low-scoring; SANA ~0.24 in-memory but not written), never losing track of the picture.
Recognizes that the ~0.24 best SANA result was never written to disk — aware of the gap, but the best alignment was NOT preserved, so it falls short of the top anchor's disciplined preservation.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains an accurate best-so-far picture per deliverable across many iterations, logs the SANA score trajectory, distinguishes slow convergence from a plateau, and abandons an approach that stopped yielding gains — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It does not reach 9-10 because it never independently scored outputs and failed to preserve the best (~0.24) alignment (killed before writing), so the 'preserves the best while exploring' requirement of the top anchor is unmet.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Recognized simple order/degree heuristics scored S3≈0.01 and abandoned them, treating the shortfall as a signal to change approach rather than grinding.
Pivoted to biological name-overlap/orthology seeding (HomoloGene); when S3≈0.0135 still failed, explicitly diagnosed that a specialized topology aligner was required and abandoned the seeding path.
Deliberate switch to SANA, an S3-optimizing topological local-search tool — a materially different tactic directly targeting the S3 shortfall (S3 low → local topological search).

Tuned the objective/parameters: killed the calibration-heavy SANA run and restarted with explicit -tinitial/-tdecay after observing wasted time; searched for precomputed alignments when it plateaued ~0.24.
Correctly used the provided reference alignment for the yeast deliverable (NC constraint), applying the right signal to the right constraint set.

After the terminal wedged, attempted blind/background SANA execution — an adaptive workaround — but steps 35-578 are otherwise non-adaptive terminal-recovery flailing, so no further metric-driven revision occurs.

dimensions.reasoning: Before the terminal broke, the agent exhibited clear level-8 behavior: it diagnosed why each metric lagged (topology S3 low → topological optimizer; NC → reference seeding), pivoted deliberately through heuristics → orthology seeding → SANA → parameter tuning, and abandoned dead ends quickly without discarding gains. It stops short of level 10 because it never combined the complementary signals into a single alignment and the entire second half of the trajectory was consumed by terminal-recovery flailing rather than continued strategy revision.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
